A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. All 31 pages of v1 and 37 pages of v3, including equations, figures and appendices, support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: Appendices D–E report original Gaussian diffusion experiments, guidance simulations, image reconstructions, latent-space analyses and mutual-information estimates.

after.justification: Section 6 and Appendices E–F report original Gaussian and image experiments, including retained results and additional covariance-flattening analyses.

M1.justification: The entropy-matching procedure, mutual-information estimator and CFG modification remain unchanged. The split-latent DAE presented prominently in v3 already appears in v1 Appendix E.2, including the split objective in Eq. (69).

E1.justification: V3 adds a nearly low-rank Gaussian input scenario by flattening selected covariance directions. The full-rank Gaussian experiments and MNIST/CIFAR-10 tasks remain; no additional real-world dataset or application domain is evaluated.

E2.justification: V3 Figure 14 adds unconditional image-model entropy curves alongside conditional curves; the corresponding v1 Figure 8 displays only conditional models. The VAE-versus-DAE and learned-versus-analytic Gaussian comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: The added flattening experiments introduce controlled covariance-eigenvalue sweeps: Figure 9 uses lambda_delta values 0.1, 0.01 and 0.001 with noise strength 1, while Figure 11 uses DX=50, DY=8 and k=10. Existing correlation sweeps, guidance experiments and image-model settings remain documented as before.

E4.justification: V3 substantially extends the analysis by separating low-dimensional input geometry from nearly deterministic conditioning. Figures 9 and 11 test whether mutual-information estimation remains accurate when neural entropy is poorly learned, and identify deterioration under extreme flattening. The split-latent and partition-time analyses already existed in v1.

E5.justification: Neither version supplies experimental run counts, random-seed information, confidence intervals or significance tests. The additional results do not introduce a new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: New Gaussian results show reasonably accurate mutual-information estimates despite missed entropy under moderate flattening, followed by estimation errors under more extreme flattening. Figure 14 newly reports unconditional neural entropy of 2017.9 and 7776.2, and image-label mutual information of 4.1 and 7.5404 nats, for MNIST and CIFAR-10 respectively. These are added estimates, not demonstrated performance gains over v1.

T1.justification: Section 6 and Appendix E.1 add a formal low-rank covariance construction and limiting analysis distinguishing divergence caused by flattening X from divergence caused by deterministic conditioning. The central entropy/MI identities, stochastic-control derivations and DAE bounds remain. The infinite-autoencoder and quantum argument is relocated rather than removed.

C1.justification: V1 foregrounds low image-label mutual information as a cause of conditioning failure and presents the quantum/autoencoder connection as a headline contribution. V3 centers the distinction between total correlation and conditioning information, and claims to explain why conditional generation and CFG remain effective despite a small MI-to-neural-entropy ratio.

C2.justification: Section 4 reverses the proposed guidance mechanism: v1 says the classification vector strengthens as a sample becomes more condition-consistent, whereas v3 says it weakens. V3 adds the explanation that divergent conditional and unconditional score components cancel, distinguishes flattening from determinism, and explicitly acknowledges difficulty validating image MI estimates. The memory-versus-compute interpretation in v1 Section 3 is removed.

D1.justification: V3 documents the flattening data-generation recipe and explicitly states that a separate DAE is trained at each partition time. V1's practical footnote describing label dropout and learned null embeddings is removed. The H200 hardware, JAX/Flax framework and embedded GitHub code link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V3 adds explicit positioning against information-theoretic diffusion work, including Kong, Dewan, Guo and Wang, and claims the first study of the interplay between total correlation and conditioning MI. Appendix D.1 adds the I-MMSE connection. Earlier positioning through memory/computation and latent diffusion, including Slepian–Wolf, Xu, Rombach and Vahdat, is removed.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion are extensively rewritten. New main-text sections emphasize manifolds and experiments, while the former DAE and infinite-tower sections move to Appendices F.1 and C. Explicit contributions and related-work passages substantially reshape the narrative.

P2.justification: V3 adds an overview plot and flattening figures, assembles main-text composite displays for guidance and latent analyses, and relocates the original introductory scatterplot to Appendix Figure 7. Figure 14 adds unconditional curves and a corresponding legend. These changes substantially reorganize the visual presentation while retaining many earlier figures.

improvement.justification: The controlled flattening-versus-determinism analysis and clearer separation of data entropy from neural entropy give v3's central argument better support than v1. The improvement is limited by unreliable new image estimates: Figure 14 reports MI values of 4.1 and 7.5404 nats, exceeding the ten-label maximum of log(10), approximately 2.303 nats, without explaining the discrepancy. The Gaussian evidence improves, but the quantitative image extension remains inadequately validated.
